newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks creep higher in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks creep higher in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks edged cautiously higher in Tuesday morning trade, lifted by a firmer tone on Wall Street overnight but amid persistent concerns about the market's future direction and interest rates, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index was up 20.74 points, or 0.17 percent, at 12,308.58. Turnover was HK$1.62 billion after the first hour of trade.
"It is a choppy market on low volume. There is not much interest in the market and it is still following Wall Street," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
The Dow industrials rose 29.84 points to 6,555.91 on Monday.
"Even though we saw a continued rebound in the U.S. market, I think the market in Hong Kong remains cautious," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
He said investors were waiting on the sidelines to see whether the downturns in both the U.S. and local markets would continue.

"At this price level, some of the blue chip shares have become quite attractive in terms of valuation but what prevents people from taking a big position in the Hong Kong market is the uncertainty coming from the U.S. market and also the property market here," said Tsang.
"People will observe the markets for a few weeks before they recommit funds to this market," he added.
Analysts said property stocks seemed to have found a short-term bottom after taking a beating on fears that the real estate market was heading for a correction.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd rose HK$0.25 to HK$78.25 and New World Development Co Ltd gained HK$0.10 to HK$41.40.
Conglomerates were weak with Hutchison Whampoa Ltd down HK$0.25 at HK$55.25 and Swire Pacific Ltd off HK$0.25 at HK$60.50.
HSBC Holdings Plc gained HK$1.00 to HK$179.50 and Hang Seng Bank Ltd was up HK$0.25 at HK$78.75.

Shares in Esprit Asia Holdings Ltd fell HK$0.125 to HK$3.525. The company said it planned to issue 180.41 million new shares to its parent Worldwide Thousand Ltd, raising net proceeds of HK$616 million.
